Triage: lands in the docs-audit script → `domain:devx`, type Bug, `pm:queue`. Rationale: same phantom-row class as **#11542** (`subroute:` / `myclient:`), which was fixed and closed **today** — this is the `$`-prefixed instance the same mechanism misses (`\b` only fails against a word character, and `$` is not one). Dispatch note: re-measure on the post-#11542 merged ref first — if its landed fix anchored all scans rather than just `declarationsIn`, this may already be absorbed; if not, apply the same pattern to the `$route:` shape and extend the fix's regression fixture with a `$`-prefixed case.

> Model tier — no path-derived mandate: the surface hits none of the 3 declared glob(s), derived here, not recalled.

**Premise re-verified on today's `main` before dispatching**, not taken from the card:

```
scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs:1410-1412
  function declLead(keys) {
    return String.raw`\b${keys}\s*:\s*`;
  }
```

The `\b` this card is about is present (landed by #11634 for #11542), and `\b` fails only against a preceding **word** character — `$` is not one. So `$route:` is still read as a declaration by all eight scans, and the phantom row this card describes is live.

⚠️ The reason this is opus rather than the floor: it is the **second population move** on the same ledger, and #11634 priced the first one at row identity (`--bridge-coverage --json` hashing `d04a5ced…` identically across base/ablated/fixed) rather than at counter equality — because this ledger's own arithmetic is what hides the defect. The same standard applies here, and widening `\b` to a negative lookbehind **also moves `declarationsIn`**, which #11634's before/after was specifically priced to leave byte-identical. That is a harder measurement than the one it inherits, not an easier one.

⚠️ Also flagged for whoever takes it: GitHub's body sanitizer strips the `<` + `!` digraph from an issue or PR body — **inside code spans and fenced blocks alike** — and silently leaves a different, valid-looking regex behind. Measured twice on PR #11634. Spell the lookbehind in the source docblock and the self-test, never in the PR body.

## Landed — PR #11710, verified by content on `origin/main`

```
5f124a219  fix(docs-audit): widen the ledger key anchor from \b to a negative lookbehind (#11710)

scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs
  function declLead(keys) { return String.raw`(?<[\w$.])${keys}\s*:\s*`; }
  "deliberately unmoved" pins   2 -> 4      (one flipped, two added; nothing deleted)
```

Card closed `completed`. `pm:dispatched` stripped.

## ⭐ This card named the wrong character class, and the fix is better for it

This report — and `declLead`'s own docblock — pointed at **`dottedRe`'s** set (word chars + `$`). The run read all three lookbehind idioms in the file and found they exclude **three different classes**:

```
symbolRe   (?<[\w$.])     word chars + $ + .     ← the right analogue: declLead's key is a BARE token
dottedRe   (?<[\w$])      word chars + $         ← what this card named
```

⭐ **And measuring it turned up a second escapee nobody had named**: a preceding `.` makes the token a member access whose colon belongs to a **ternary** —

```
cond ? obj.route : 'X'
```

— minting the same phantom row through a different piece of syntax. A fix built to this card's spec would have shipped with that still open. Closed and pinned.

`-` was deliberately left **out** with the reason stated: `a-route` is two tokens, so `route` genuinely *is* the whole token — it is not a declaration for a different reason, one it shares with the bare `cond ? route : x` that no lookbehind can reach. Declining a case with a reason beats closing it by reflex.

## The pricing standard this card set was met, on both populations

- **Population 1 (ledger rows), at row identity**: `--bridge-coverage --json` hashed `d04a5ced…` on base, ablated **and** fixed; set difference 0 in each direction.
- **Population 2 (`declarationsIn`)** — the one #11542's before/after was deliberately priced to leave byte-identical, and the reason this card was filed separately rather than folded in. Measured by slicing `declarationsIn` plus its dependency closure — **walked, not hand-listed** — and running the file's own bodies over the seven live ledgers: 491 declarations, hash identical on all three trees.
- ⭐ **The positive control ran BEFORE the zero was believed**: over a synthetic ledger carrying both escapees the same harness reports 5 vs 3 and names exactly the two that disappear. That ordering is the whole difference between a measurement and a hope.
- **"Free on today's tree" re-derived, not inherited**: 499 live leads, every one preceded by a space — 0 by `$`, 0 by `.`, 0 by any non-word char, with its own control.
- ⭐ **The subset invariant was swept, not argued**: over code points `0..0x2FFF` the old anchor admits 12225, the new 12223, and the new admits **0** the old did not. Exactly two characters move. Both numbers pinned.

## The self-test caught the implementer, and the response was right

The first probe draft compiled `declLead` directly and tripped the *"all eight lead scans, none inline"* pin (expected 8, got 9). It **rebuilt the probe rather than bumping the pin to 9** — bumping would have gone green in a minute at the cost of blunting the only thing that can catch a real ninth scan. Reporting that unprompted is why the rest of the report reads as credible.

## Follow-on

This card's **option 3** — a whole-token key allowlist retiring the family rather than shrinking it once more — is now **#11717**, filed with #11630's own measurement as the affordability argument (499/499 leads preceded by a space ⇒ an allowlist is free on today's tree by the same reasoning every lookbehind card used). **#11711** (the Unicode residue, `\w` being ASCII-only) is `pm:blocked` behind it as subsumed.

⚠️ For the record: the implementer flagged the allowlist choice as a maintainer call. It is not — it is an implementation-approach choice on this lane's own surface with the deciding measurement already taken, so this seat made it rather than adding it to the maintainer's queue.
